summary: One supported capacity-lifetime defect in the connector-boundaries working-tree snapshot: timed-out HTTP/TLS and redirect lookups can remain in flight after connector slots are released. Public/private target checks, scan confinement and incomplete-scan signaling otherwise had no supported findings within the reviewed scope. 195 existing focused/API/auth/startup tests passed, and two isolated stalled-DNS reproductions passed their defect assertions.
coverage: Fresh independent native review from review-brief.txt, without implementer conclusions; effective AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md, project/workflow/invariants, phase-2 milestone 1 connector contract and relevant README/architecture sections examined.

Reviewed current dirty source, not HEAD: complete auth/egress.ts and connectors/index.ts, limits.ts, network.ts, web-posture.ts, repo-scan.ts. Traced literal and all-answer DNS classification, redirect validation/count/downgrade, encoded/decoded response limits, HTTP/TLS abort and resource lifetime, shared concurrency, root allowlists, symlink/special-file handling, read/entry/time limits and incomplete secrets output.

Examined context.ts/server.ts operator-root integration; VisuaService constructor, createConnector/runConnector, requirement mapping, transactional mutation/audit/evidence and agent connector caller; app.ts error mapping and connector routes; auth/http.ts tenant middleware and AuthService.oidcFor private-provider transport integration.

Examined related connector-boundaries, egress-dns, egress and repo-scan test files; relevant API/startup/auth cases and documentation. Ran pnpm exec vitest run apps/server/test/connector-boundaries.test.ts apps/server/test/egress-dns.test.ts apps/server/test/egress.test.ts apps/server/test/repo-scan.test.ts apps/server/test/startup.test.ts apps/server/test/api.test.ts: 6 files, 162 tests passed. Ran pnpm exec vitest run apps/server/test/auth.test.ts: 1 file, 33 tests passed, including tenant access and operator-approved private OIDC providers.

Ran isolated review-vitest.config.ts against review-dns-lifetime.test.ts: 2 tests passed. With actual registry/web/HTTP/TLS code and only node:dns.lookup callbacks withheld, three cancelled four-run batches admitted 12 unresolved lookups; accelerated configured network/run deadline batches admitted further runs while earlier lookup callbacks remained outstanding. No external host connection was made; cleanup completed withheld callbacks with ENOTFOUND.

Bound reviewed inputs to review-scope.json at HEAD c8a1ed06a8043fe725381ccccd89779b6a3498e0. SHA-256 comparison found every recorded input unchanged except README.md, whose reviewed refinement had SHA-256 8c72c49fc005b84fde6a572f19a56e2a34174285e44e46e2373bd81a152a8607 and clarified pending filesystem capacity retention. Source was not edited by this reviewer.

findings.mechanism: A slow or stuck connection-time dns.lookup remains live after request/socket abort or redirect preflight abort rejects its awaiting promise. guardedLookup does not expose or track callback completion; connector work can consequently finish and decrement active before its resolver work stops. Repeated tenant connector runs are admitted even though earlier unresolved lookups still occupy or queue resolver work. The 12-second operation deadline can also cause later probes in the same run to start additional lookups while earlier ones remain pending. This violates the explicit requirement to retain process capacity until underlying work stops and can exhaust resolver capacity under a stalled resolver.
findings.evidence: review-dns-lifetime.test.ts uses the real createConnectorKinds([]) web-posture registry entry, guarded HTTP/TLS code and budget, replacing only node:dns.lookup with callbacks held until cleanup. Its first passing reproduction admits three successive four-run batches after caller cancellation while all 12 DNS callbacks remain outstanding. Its second passing reproduction accelerates the actual requested 30000/12000 ms policies to 120/45 ms, lets natural deadlines expire, and confirms a second four-run batch is admitted while at least eight callbacks from the first batch remain unresolved and the total grows by at least eight. review-dns-lifetime.log records 2 passing reproduction tests. Static source confirms DNS callbacks are separate from request error rejection and active decreases only on kind.run promise settlement.
findings.recommendation: Track the lifetime of every guarded DNS lookup started by a connector, including socket lookups and redirect preflight, and retain its connector capacity slot until all those callbacks have completed in addition to connector task cleanup. Preserve the separate bounded caller deadline. Add a stalled-lookup regression that verifies new runs receive capacity refusal after old callers time out until pending DNS callbacks finish.

limitations: DNS failure was simulated with withheld node:dns.lookup callbacks; the operating-system resolver itself was not intentionally stalled. Policy-deadline reproduction used accelerated durations while asserting the requested production limits.
Existing suites ran on local SQLite with local mock IdPs; PostgreSQL, browser e2e and the full pnpm check were not rerun by this focused reviewer. Running Docker and external hosts were not accessed.

Filesystem ancestor replacement and noncancellable kernel filesystem stalls remain the explicitly documented operator-controlled-root/runtime constraints in the brief; the review did not induce those kernel conditions.
This report describes the stable snapshot read during the first independent pass. Any integration-owner fixes made afterward require focused revalidation and are not included in this verdict.
